text:
sanjay: Heads-up: I'm digging into tenant->region/tier binding for fallback decisions. The policy DSL today only has a single score path (weights + penalties) and it's getting awkward to express "hard affinity" vs "soft penalty". cc @lina @ethan
lina: +1 saw this in the canary. We're losing important semantics when policy compiler flattens everything into a single weight. Operators want deterministic bindings for some tenants.
ethan: Can you sketch the two behaviors you need? hard affinity = never route out of region unless absolutely unavailable? soft = allow but add cost penalty?
sanjay: Exactly. Two examples: 1) Bank tenant must stay in eu-west unless outage -> hard affinity. 2) Mobile game tenant prefers us-east for latency but can be routed globally with +0.2 cost penalty -> soft affinity.
maria: Important: our runtime needs to be cheap. We can't run complex constraint solves per request. Whatever representation we pick must be precomputable and constant-time at the router.
kevin: What about split responsibility: compiler emits a compact compatibility mask for each (tenant, route) and router uses bitops + precomputed penalty table? That keeps runtime checks O(1).
lina: I like the mask idea. Also need to preserve ordering for fallbacks (priority lists). A mask doesn't encode order by itself.
ethan: We can emit two things from compiler: (1) ordered candidate list (small, e.g. top-5) and (2) compatibility bitmask for quick membership tests. Router tries list in order, falls back to bitmask search if order exhausted.
sanjay: Here's a draft DSL snippet to show intent:```policy "tenant:fancygames" { prefer { region: "us-east-1" priority: 0 } fallback { regions: ["us-west-2","eu-west-1"] penalty: 0.2 ordered: true } hard_affinity { region: "eu-west-1" enforce_on: ["banking-123"] } }```
maria: Two questions: a) how do we signal "enforce_on" (tenant set) at compile time? b) what's the semantics when both prefer and hard_affinity exist?
kevin: Compiler will expand tenant groups into per-tenant compiled config. If a tenant has a hard_affinity entry, compiler will mark its primary candidate as 'pinned' and set pin_ttl and pin_on_miss behavior. Prefer + hard_affinity means prefer wins for general traffic, but for tenants in the enforce_on list, treat as hard bind.
lina: Pin TTL matters for cache invalidation. If we pin a tenant to a node/region for X minutes, on config changes we must invalidate quickly or risk stale binds. Suggest default pin_ttl=5m and support a forced flush route in console.
ethan: Ops-bot note: deploy-bot will need to emit rollout events so we can track which tenants got new compiled configs. ops-bot: triggered rollout event when new policy compiles -> we should include per-tenant checksum in the event.
sanjay: Migration plan idea: phase 1 = compiler emits both legacy weight vector + new compatibility artifacts (ordered list + mask). Router reads legacy if new absent. Phase 2 = switch default to new path then remove legacy after 2 weeks.
maria: Perf numbers required. Can we get a microbench of bitmask membership + checking ordered list vs full solver? If bitmask + ordered list hits 99.9% then it's good.
kevin: I'll create a short benchmark: 100k requests/s emulation, candidate pools of 8 regions, top-5 ordered lists. Expect per-request cost ~ few ns for mask ops + a couple memory lookups.
lina: Edge case: cross-tenant pooling. If multiple tenants are co-located and a node needs preemption, hard binds might block useful packing. Consider a preemptible flag on hard_affinity so we can collapse to soft if capacity low.
sanjay: Good point. Add `preemptible: true/false` to the DSL. Also add `fallback_quota` to avoid over-saturating fallback regions.
maria: Action items: 1) kevin => benchmark mask+ordered approach (due EOD Wed) 2) sanjay => formalize DSL additions and produce compiler emit examples (due Fri) 3) lina => list cache/pin TTL options and invalidation story (due Fri) 4) eth an => propose console UX for forced flush + per-tenant checksum events (due Mon)
kevin: I'll post benchmark results in this thread.
ethan: Thanks. If benchmarks look good, I can start a small RFC patch for the policy compiler.
sanjay: Thanks all. tagging this as follow-up for the routing-policy epic. :thumbsup:
